candidates.rationale: F60 represents num/60^scale. reduce removes the full gcd from num but only removes whole powers of 60 from scale: (2,1) becomes (1,1), changing 1/30 to 1/60. BA.EXACT can construct this value from 2/60. This is an arithmetic correctness defect in the CLI interpreter, independently of any security claim.

source_checks.observation: Constructor always reduces; denominator representation is 60^scale.
Division scales numerator then constructs F60 from quotient and scale.

guards: Zero numerator is normalized safely; this guard does not protect nonzero partial base factors.
Division-by-zero and scale>20 halt guards do not detect value-changing reduction.

candidates.rationale: BA.EXACT divides using val2.num only and retains the dividend scale; it never multiplies by 60^val2.scale. A divisor obtained by 1/60 has (num=1,scale=1); dividing integer 1 by it returns (1,0) instead of (60,0). This is independent of the partial-gcd reduction issue because gcd(1,60)=1.

source_checks.observation: Register expression returns both numerator and scale.
Divisor scale is unused throughout BA.EXACT.

guards: Zero divisor numerator rejected; expansion limited to scale 20. Neither guard enforces divisor-scale semantics.

guards: Malformed numeric suffix defaults to register 0, which is not an arity or range guard.

candidates.rationale: The current TLOAD constant evaluates to 0x5e and analyze_bytecode counts that byte. Counts feed transient-storage risk findings and the orchestrator receipt threshold.

guards: PUSH-data exclusion avoids one false-positive class but cannot correct an incorrect opcode constant.

candidates.rationale: from_address shifts away the low 146 bits before masking. Address 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000080 is decoded as zero here despite that flag. Resulting risk findings/receipt selection can be wrong.

candidates.rationale: from_decimal narrows value/3600 from u64 to u32 without range checking. At value=3600*2^32 the high limb becomes zero and lower limbs are zero, so conversion returns zero. saturating_add saturates only the u64 intermediate then uses the same narrowing conversion, so adding one to maximum canonical three-limb value wraps instead of saturating its representation.

source_checks.observation: Unchecked narrowing conversion and public arithmetic delegation.
Add/Sub trait operations use those arithmetic methods.

guards: Modulo normalization bounds the two low limbs; it does not bound the high limb.
u64 saturation does not enforce the lower representable F60 maximum.

candidates.rationale: Two balls with mid=0 and rad=u32::MAX each include u32::MAX. Their sum must include 2*u32::MAX, representable in the public u64 bound domain. add_ball saturates the output radius to u32::MAX and leaves mid=0, so contains(2*u32::MAX) is false. The claimed rigorous enclosure is lost; this counterexample does not depend on midpoint overflow.

source_checks.observation: Public radius is u32; bounds are u64; sum radius saturates.
Subtraction uses the same finite-radius saturation.
Arithmetic trait methods expose these routines.

guards: saturating_add avoids integer overflow but under-approximates required uncertainty.
